game.title: Indianapolis Colts at Kansas City Chiefs

lede: Indianapolis Colts carries the stronger EdgeDesk offensive profile (#16 in EPA per play), while Kansas City Chiefs owns the more favourable defensive matchup (#11 in EPA allowed per play).
EdgeDesk’s independent projection makes it Kansas City Chiefs -0.1 with a fair total of 44.8 — approximately a one-score game, before any sportsbook number is consulted.

The widest measured matchup on the board is Indianapolis Colts pass offence vs Kansas City Chiefs pass defence, which sits −0.047 from the league mean once the two ratings are combined the way the model combines them.
The largest uncertainty is availability: NFL injury report — not loaded in this session.

score.note: Split from EdgeDesk’s own fair spread and fair total, rounded to whole points. It is the centre of a distribution, not a prediction of the exact score.

moneyline.note: EdgeDesk’s own fair price, with no margin in it. It is not a quote and nobody offers it.

outcome_range.note: Quoted from the perspective of Kansas City Chiefs, off the engine’s own learned margin distribution (conditioned on this spread, so real key-number mass is kept). Eight results in ten land inside p10–p90.

projection.confidence_absent_reason: The NFL model publishes no single confidence score. What it publishes instead is the width of the outcome range above and the sample the ratings rest on: the trained seeds through 2025, plus 15 absorbed 2026 games.
projection.status_note: EdgeDesk differs from the market by 6.4 points. That is enough to look harder — and out of sample no gap size of any width has cleared p<0.05 against the close, so it is a research prompt and not an edge.
projection.validation: UNPROVEN — this model does NOT beat the closing line out of sample. Research only; nothing here is graded as a bet.
